---
title: SpectralMDL
subtitle: A spectral, LLVM-based JIT compiler for the Material Definition Language
---

SpectralMDL compiles materials written in NVIDIA's
[Material Definition Language](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/design-visualization/technologies/material-definition-language)
(MDL) to native code, and is intended to be useful as a middleware C++
library in offline physically-based rendering programs. It is developed at
the [Digital Imaging and Remote Sensing (DIRS)](https://www.rit.edu/dirs)
laboratory at the Rochester Institute of Technology in support of the
[DIRSIG](http://dirsig.cis.rit.edu) simulation tool.

## Features

- **Spectral.** A `color` is a spectrum of wavelength samples, 16 by
  default, rather than an RGB triple.
- **Just-in-time compiled.** Modules are parsed, emitted as LLVM-IR, and
  compiled to native code with LLVM's ORC JIT.
- **The MDL standard library.** The builtin modules, such as `::df`,
  `::math`, `::state`, and `::tex`, are embedded in the library.
- **Resources.** Images, spectra, measured BSDFs, light profiles, and voxel
  grids, with optional Ptex and NanoVDB support.
- **Renderer utilities.** Monte Carlo sampling, a sun-sky model, and
  manifold next-event estimation, usable by any renderer.
- **The SMDL dialect.** A module that opens with `#smdl` gains intrinsics,
  attributes, unit tests, `defer`, and more, and can add its own
  distributions beside the builtin ones.

## Building

SpectralMDL needs a C++17 compiler, CMake 3.28 or newer, and LLVM 22.1 or
newer. Ptex and NanoVDB, which are on by default, are fetched and built
along with it.

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/path/to/llvm
ninja -C build
ctest --test-dir build
```

| Option | Default | Effect |
|---------------------|----------|---------------------------------------|
| `SMDL_BUILD_LLVM` | `OFF` | Build LLVM rather than find an installed one. |
| `SMDL_ENABLE_PTEX` | `ON` | Build with Ptex integration. |
| `SMDL_ENABLE_NANOVDB` | `ON` | Build with NanoVDB integration. |
| `SMDL_RTTI` | `ON` | Build with C++ run-time type information. |
| `SMDL_CXX_NATIVE` | `OFF` | Compile for the build machine's CPU, at the cost of portability. |
| `SMDL_INSTALL` | top level only | Generate install rules. |

Turning off both `SMDL_ENABLE_PTEX` and `SMDL_ENABLE_NANOVDB` lowers the
CMake requirement to 3.21.

## Using the library

An installed SpectralMDL is found as a CMake package. Its version check
accepts only the exact version requested.

```cmake
find_package(SpectralMDL REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(renderer PRIVATE SpectralMDL::SpectralMDL)
```

A host adds modules to a [`Compiler`](doxygen/html/classsmdl_1_1Compiler.html),
compiles them, and looks up the materials it wants. Each step that can fail
returns an `std::optional<smdl::Error>`. Errors and warnings go to the
library's logger, which prints nothing until the host gives it a sink.

```cpp
#include "smdl/Compiler.h"
#include "smdl/Support/Logger.h"

smdl::Logger::get().addSink<smdl::LogSinks::PrintToCerr>();
smdl::Compiler compiler;
if (auto error = compiler.add("materials")) // A file or a directory
  error->printAndExit();
if (auto error = compiler.compile())
  error->printAndExit();
if (auto error = compiler.jitCompile())
  error->printAndExit();
const smdl::jit::MaterialDef *materialDef = compiler.findMaterial("glass");
```

The host then evaluates a [`jit::Material`](doxygen/html/structsmdl_1_1jit_1_1Material.html)
from the [`jit::MaterialDef`](doxygen/html/structsmdl_1_1jit_1_1MaterialDef.html)
at each shading point. JIT-compiled code points into data the `Compiler`
owns, and calling `compile()` again invalidates every function pointer
taken from the previous compile.

## The `smdl` program

The library comes with a command-line program, `smdl`, with these
subcommands.

| Subcommand | Purpose |
|-------------|------------------------------------------------|
| `smdl doc` | Show documentation. |
| `smdl dump` | Dump as LLVM-IR or native assembly. |
| `smdl format` | Format source code. |
| `smdl list` | List all materials. |
| `smdl run` | Run execs. |
| `smdl test` | Run execs and unit tests. |
| `smdl volume` | Convert voxel grids between `.vol` and `.nvdb`. |

Environment variables such as `SMDL_DUMP_IR` and `SMDL_OPT_LEVEL` debug a
compile without the host program's help. The
[README](https://github.com/mgradysaunders/SpectralMDL#environment-variables)
lists them.

## API reference

The [API reference](doxygen/html/index.html) is generated from the headers
with Doxygen, and is organized into these groups.

- [Compiler](doxygen/html/group__compiler.html): turning MDL source code
  into native code, and the `jit` interface that materials are called
  through.
- [Resources](doxygen/html/group__resource.html): images, spectra, measured
  BSDFs, light profiles, scene data, and the shading `State`.
- [Render Utilities](doxygen/html/group__renderutil.html): spectral
  containers, Monte Carlo sampling, illuminants, and the sun-sky model.
- [Manifold](doxygen/html/group__manifold.html): manifold next-event
  estimation and specular manifold sampling.
- [Abstract Syntax Tree](doxygen/html/group__ast.html): the parsed
  representation of an MDL module.
- [Support](doxygen/html/group__support.html): math, strings, files,
  logging, hashing, random numbers, and allocation.
